title: Harun al-Rashid and the Incorruptible Judge

full_text:
A citizen of Baghdad brought a property lawsuit against one of Caliph Harun al-Rashid’s imperial treasurers before the bench of Judge Abdullah bin Nafi'. The Caliph sent an imperial chamberlain with a royal message, suggesting that the court dismiss the suit in the state’s favor.

Judge Abdullah looked upon the imperial messenger with grave solemnity:

'Tell the Commander of the Faithful: In this courtroom, the Emperor and the water-carrier stand upon the exact same level before the balance of justice! If the Caliph wishes to be judged by the law of heaven, let his treasurer produce verified deeds, or let him restore the citizen’s property.'

The judge ruled in favor of the humble citizen and ordered the treasurer to make restitution.

The courtiers trembled, expecting the Caliph to execute the defiant judge.

Harun al-Rashid summoned Judge Abdullah to the palace. The Caliph stood from his throne, embraced the judge, and declared before all the emirs:

'Blessed is the empire where a judge fears truth more than the Emperor’s sword! As long as Abdullah bin Nafi' sits upon the bench, my realm is safe from tyranny.' The Caliph confirmed the judgment and made Abdullah Chief Justice of the empire.
moral: An upright magistrate who stands firm on the law even before the Emperor commands royal reverence.
